evidence: Single application entry point (bot.py) with explicit imports from modules (config, pyrogram), indicating a unified runtime
Clear separation into logical modules: database, helper_funcs, plugins, config, translation — each encapsulating cohesive responsibilities
No external service boundaries or inter-process communication (no network calls between modules, no REST/gRPC usage in code)
Shared dependencies (e.g., database modules used directly via import, translation shared across plugins)
All code in single repository with flat top-level structure and ≤2 directory depth, typical of maintainable monoliths
Fan-out of 6.4 suggests high interdependency but not tight coupling; consistent with modular monolith where modules depend on shared utilities/services
Use of global config class (Config) and shared translation suggests centralized configuration and localization within one process
risks: Tight coupling between plugins and core infrastructure (e.g., direct imports of database modules in plugins) may reduce testability and modularity over time
Lack of explicit layers (e.g., service/domain layer abstraction) could blur separation of concerns between business logic and I/O
High fan-out suggests dependencies may become circular or hard to manage as project grows without explicit dependency rules
